verdicts: Q1 LOOP-DEFER ORACLE — SETTLED: gen2 at-most-once flag model is the sole canonical semantics. DeferStmt registers the body once at COMPILE time and emits only an idempotent `__defer_N_active = 1;` (self/codegen.hexa:3526-3531, verified); drain runs each body at most once under its flag at __fn_exit with drain-time variable values (self/codegen.hexa:2275-2289, verified). The interp's per-iteration push (N executions) is moot: self/hexa_full.hexa was DELETED at ab7015fa1 (2026-05-19, 'R7 Cycle C step-1 — delete interpreter source, 25,548 lines', verified via git log). The plan's contingency 'interp가 갈리면 별도 byte-neutral PR로 정렬' (state/hexa-own/M1_defer_wiring.md 미결 §1) is DEAD — there is nothing to align and it would have been byteeq-invisible anyway (.github/workflows/selfhost-byteeq-gate.yml compares compiler-generation objects only). CAVEAT: gen2's own comment at self/codegen.hexa:3528-3530 claims it 'matches the interp interpreter's defer_stack.push behavior' — TRUE only for the unreached-defer case, FALSE for loop multiplicity; M1 docs must state the flag model on its own terms, not as interp-parity.

Q2 FN-EXIT vs PER-BLOCK — SETTLED: fn-exit only. gen2 emits exactly one __fn_exit label per fn with the drain and arena return there (self/codegen.hexa:2267-2295, verified: forced fall-through goto at ~2273, reverse-registration drain, `return __hexa_fn_arena_return(__ret_val)`); explicit return routes `__ret_val = …; goto __fn_exit;` only when _gen2_defer_flag_count > 0 (self/codegen.hexa:~3498-3505, verified — non-defer fns keep the zero-overhead direct return). break/continue/inner-block exits never drain. THROW never drains: ThrowStmt → hexa_throw (self/codegen.hexa:~3844) = hxlcl_longjmp to the caller's hxlcl_setjmp try frame, bypassing __fn_exit entirely — canonical M1-out-of-scope semantics, pinned by test as must-NOT-fire. Per-block drain would be a shipping-behavior change requiring its own byteeq+smoke decision; not M1.

Q3 DEFER-ASSIGNMENT LEGALITY — SETTLED: REJECT, matching gen2, but the naive native port would silently ACCEPT it. Verified: gen2 parse_expr has no `=` level (self/parser.hexa:3083-3095 — only walrus ColonEq; assignment is stmt-level AssignStmt at self/parser.hexa:1508-1520), so gen2 `defer x = 1` parses `x`, leaves `=` unconsumed, and the dangling assignment errors downstream. Native parse_expr == parse_assignment (compiler/parse/parser.hexa:480-481) and parse_assignment consumes Eq/PlusEq/MinusEq/StarEq/SlashEq into ExprKind::Assign (parser.hexa:488-506, verified) — so the native defer expr-form MUST call parse_logical_or() (the level directly below assignment) instead of parse_expr(), then diag if next token ∈ {Eq, PlusEq, MinusEq, StarEq, SlashEq}. Use the NATIVE 5-token set only — gen2's wider compound set (PercentEq/PowerEq/ShlEq/... at self/parser.hexa:1500) has no counterpart in compiler/lex/tokens.hexa.

Q4 CONTEXTUAL GATE SHAPE — SETTLED: explicit TokenKind whitelist is MANDATORY, not just recommended. Verified: parse_primary never rejects — it consumes ANY unrecognized token and returns a placeholder Ident (compiler/parse/parser.hexa:1156-1166), so a try-parse gate is structurally impossible. tokens.hexa has zero KwDefer (grep verified) — `defer` lexes as Ident; gate = stmt-position Ident(text=='defer') AND next ∈ {LBrace, Number, String, Char, KwTrue, KwFalse, PNode, CNode, LNode, ENode, Ident, Bang, Tilde, KwIf, KwWhile, KwFor, KwMatch, KwTry, KwThrow, KwFn, HashLBrace, LParen}. Ambiguous tokens resolve to identifier-use (EXCLUDED): Minus (`defer - 1` binop), Pipe/PipePipe (`defer | x` — cost: pipe-closure form `defer |x| body` rejected, a divergence from gen2's hard keyword), LBracket (`defer[i]` index). LParen included (matches gen2 `defer (expr)`, self/parser.hexa:4756-4765; corpus has zero code identifiers named `defer`). Hard-keyword promotion stays rejected per state/rfc_reseed_canonical_keywords.md contextual-sanction.

CARRIER CORRECTION (affects plan Step 1 wording): the match_guard precedent rides ExprKind::If + text=='match_guard' (compiler/parse/ast.hexa:172-178, verified), NOT ExprKind::Block as the plan implies — but the Block+text carrier is still viable: Block lowering passes e.text verbatim into _mk_hexpr (compiler/lower/ast_to_hir.hexa:1954, verified) and all three check passes are transparent to Block .text (resolve.hexa:195-211 kind-agnostic walk · bind.hexa:945-954 scope push/walk/pop · types.hexa:1926-1957 child iteration, Wall A HEXA_STATIC_TYPES slice reads only child-let .text). Exhaustive-match ripple = exactly 93 sites (grep 'ExprKind::Throw ->' == 93, verified), so the no-new-ExprKind rule stands.

STALE PLAN ROW: M1_defer_wiring.md's executor table lists 'interp (hexa run) ✅ per-call defer_stack' — STALE. `hexa run` is compile-then-exec gen2 (interp retired R7, g_interp_deprecated in self/main.hexa); only TWO lanes exist (gen2 C-transpile default + aprime opt-in). Step 0 and Step 5's '3 실행기' language must become 2-lane.
